newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore not seen as Asia's trade gateway - survey.
newsitem.headline: Singapore not seen as Asia's trade gateway - survey.

text.p: Most of Singapore's neighbours do not share the island state's view of itself as Asia's trading gateway, according to a report issued on Thursday.

When it comes to the region's two biggest potential markets -- India and China -- Singapore fails to make an impact with Asian exporters, said the DHL-Gallup Quarterly Export Indicator survey of 15 countries in the Asia-Pacific region.
"Singapore exporters clearly perceive the country as being the trading gateway to China, while the majority of exporters in 12 of the 15 countries did not," it said.
Only Indonesia cited Singapore as its gateway to India and China. "No other country sees Singapore in this way," the survey said.
The survey only asked whether respondents thought of Singapore as Asia's trade gateway. It did not ask about alternatives.

Pollsters questioned more than 1,100 business leaders and found pessimism among exporters in Japan, Korea and China, revealed a growing acceptance of Australia as part of Asia, and named Europe as a major target market for Asian exporters.
"In both the long-term (five years) and the short-term (next 12 months), cost and trade atmosphere were cited as the most important factors influencing export sales," the survey said.
Respondents said India, China and Vietnam were the most difficult countries to initiate trade with, while Singapore and Hong Kong were the easiest.
A major inhibitor to exports was the shortage of skilled labour in the region, the survey found.
"This is especially so in Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, Taiwan and China where more than six in 10 respondents perceived the problem," the survey said.
